remaining_mandatory_behavior.gap: Deterministically select actual recovery Stop report completion first, then inject the superseding control before recovery clears the original first-control deadline, with pendingControl still nil; force a following protected operation to remain blocked and assert the original 3s limit.
remaining_mandatory_behavior.reason: The existing real after-commit report barrier holds the subprocess while Run is in await. Injecting control before releasing it deterministically allows await's control-first branch. Releasing it with controlWake pending makes two Go select cases ready; the selected case is unspecified, not controllable by inputStarter. The starter exposes admit/emit but no completion observation after await has selected the actual result and before the recovery epoch commit. No assertion can honestly distinguish which branch ran using the current external outputs alone. Timing sleeps, GOMAXPROCS/scheduling assumptions or repeated random attempts would not meet the requested deterministic interleaving.
remaining_mandatory_behavior.minimal_engineer_request: Expose an unexported optional observation/barrier immediately after the actual recovery Stop await returns successfully and before the pendingControl/ifCurrent recovery finalization, keeping public Run/runWithTranscript defaults unchanged. Test can hold real Stop after commit, preserve the first-control timestamp, complete that actual report, stop at this post-await boundary, inject the real interrupt via inputStarter, then resume into the actual epoch-owned finalization and block the next protected input_control Sync using existing recordBarrier. This guarantees completion-first/pendingControl-nil ordering without replacing controller logic. Engineer may choose an equally narrow existing-boundary alternative if it exposes the same ordering.
